title: Melanie Oyarzun
text:
I am a Chilean researcher based in Budapest, currently a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the Center for Collective Learning (Corvinus University of Budapest).
My work combines social network analysis, applied microeconometrics, and experimental methods to study social integration, inequality, and learning contexts.
Explore my research →

title: Autism shapes social integration and reciprocity in elementary classrooms
text:
Storytelling (Closeread prototype)




Step 1. Why this paper
Inclusion in classrooms depends not only on attendance but on social interaction patterns between peers.




Step 2. Network lens
We study how students are socially integrated and how reciprocity differs across social profiles.




Step 3. Empirical signal
The paper documents systematic differences in integration and reciprocal ties, which matter for learning environments.




Step 4. Why it matters
Results can guide practical interventions for more inclusive classrooms and peer support structures.

Main contribution

title: About
text:
I am a Postdoctoral Research Fellow at the Center for Collective Learning. My research interests include:

computational social science
social networks and reciprocity
cooperation and inequality
education policy and peer effects
applied microeconometrics

I completed a PhD in Social Complexity Sciences (Universidad del Desarrollo), and hold an MSc in Economics (Pontificia Universidad Catolica de Chile).
